messages:
rahul: quick flag — we're trying to onboard muse-13b-v1. upstream license says "NonCommercial + NoRedistribute". what does that block?

lena_legal: short version: it prevents us from distributing weights or derivatives and limits commercial use. details depend on author intent; need to confirm. paste exact license text?

rahul: repo README: ```Usage: Personal & Research only. No commercial use. Redistribution of weights and derivatives prohibited.```

sam: pragmatic Q: our Dedicated/Private customers expect the weights in their infra. wouldn't that be redistribution?

lena_legal: yes. handing weights to customers is redistribution. even shipping quantized weights counts as a derivative and so is restricted under "derivatives prohibited."

jordan: so quantization = derivative? that prevents us from providing optimized artifacts to customers?

lena_legal: generally yes. Transformations like quantization, pruning, conversion are viewed as derivatives. We need an explicit exception from the licensor to provide transformed weights.

emily: product impact: Private and BYO on-prem flows would be blocked unless customers obtain rights themselves. Hosted inference might still be an issue because of "non-commercial" clause.

rahul: If we keep the model internal for eval only, can we run experiments and report metrics internally?

lena_legal: internal, non-public evals under research use are lower risk, but avoid exposing it to customers and don't publish artifacts. mark all artifacts as quarantined and limit access.

sam: engineering note: we can implement catalog metadata flags to prevent blocked deployment modes. e.g., tags: distribution_allowed=false, commercial_use_allowed=false. Then UI can hide Dedicated/Private.

jordan: ML ops: for evals we'll run inside a sealed sandbox. No weight exports, no quantized binaries leave the environment. Logs only; strip any binary blobs from archives before saving.

emily: could we do BYOW (bring-your-own-weights) where customers supply the weights and we provide installation scripts and configs but never touch the files?

lena_legal: BYOW is safer because we don't redistribute. Two caveats: 1) customers must confirm they have rights to provide weights; 2) our onboarding artifacts must not include any weight files. Add a legal acknowledgement checkbox in the flow.

rahul: about attribution: license asks for author attribution on derivatives. If we only host inference internally, do we still need to display attribution in the Console and model card?

lena_legal: yes. Attribution obligations generally survive even for hosted use. Add author, model name, and license link to the model card and include a short attribution snippet users can copy.

sam: ops action: block deploy paths for models with these flags; add telemetry event if an internal eval uses the model so we can trace accidental exposures.

jordan: ML action: run quantization-only experiments but never persist quantized weights externally. If upstream clarifies that quantized artifacts are allowed, then we can revisit.

lena_legal: I'll draft a concise outreach template requesting clarification and optionally a commercial license or redistribution exception. Hold off on customer-facing delivery until we have written permission.

deploy-bot: deployment-checklist: muse-13b-v1 quarantined for internal-eval-only. artifact-export disabled.

emily: next steps summarized: legal to reach out; eng to add catalog flags + UI banner; ML to run sandboxed evals and purge artifacts; product to prepare BYOW docs and attribution copy. I'll open a short ticket to track.

rahul: thanks all — keeping notes here for the onboarding doc. :thumbsup:
